supporting_observations.claim: At 13:49:51 UTC, a Zeek HTTP connection from FILE-ORC-01 (10.56.20.20) to 10.56.20.30:8080 transferred 640,000,532 bytes from the host and received 39,150 bytes. This establishes a large transfer to the proxy, not the ultimate Internet destination.

The observed volume is compatible with the several-hundred-MB Keystone backup upload described in the inventory, but the available flow record does not identify the Keystone agent or establish that this was a backup.
The logged large transfer occurred at 13:49:51 UTC, several minutes after the alert's approximate 13:46 time; the supplied records do not establish whether this is exactly the alerted flow.

known_telemetry_limitations: FILE-ORC-01 winsec and Sysmon collection was unavailable from 13:30 to 14:15 UTC, so process, account, and file activity for the transfer window cannot be verified.
PROXY-ORC-01 proxy-log collection was unavailable from 13:30 to 14:15 UTC, leaving the proxied destination and request details unobserved.
Zeek connection telemetry was available, but the supplied flow record identifies only the internal proxy endpoint, not the ultimate destination or transferred content.
claims_not_established: Whether the transfer was generated by the approved Keystone backup agent or another process.
The ultimate destination, URL, or service reached through the proxy.
What data was transferred, whether it was authorized, or whether it contained sensitive information.
Whether the 13:49:51 flow is the exact connection that triggered the alert described as occurring around 13:46 UTC.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover FILE-ORC-01 Sysmon and Windows security logs for 13:30–14:15 UTC, especially process and network activity associated with the transfer.
Obtain PROXY-ORC-01 access logs for the transfer to identify the requested destination, account, and request details.
Review Keystone agent and scheduled-job logs, including upload timing, destination, and byte counts, and compare them with the observed flow.
Obtain the alert's exact flow identifiers and timestamps to correlate it with the 13:49:51 Zeek connection.
unrelated_findings: A successful RDP logon to FILE-ORC-01 by tess.hart from WS-THART-01 is recorded at 13:21 UTC. The inventory says remote administration is only performed from WS-SBYRNE-01; investigate separately. This does not establish a connection to the alerted transfer. Records: T270-00010, T270-00015, T270-00017, T270-00021.

FILE-ORC-01 connected to DC-ORC-01 over TCP/5985 (WS-Man) at 13:52 UTC. This is an unusual management-protocol connection in light of the stated remote-administration practice and merits separate review; the available record does not link it to the transfer. Records: T270-00317, T270-00318, T270-00319.

A Zeek record shows an SSH connection from FILE-ORC-01 to PROXY-ORC-01 on port 22 at 14:18 UTC. SSH is not among the approved services in the supplied inventory; investigate separately. The record alone does not establish successful authentication or a relationship to the alert. Record: T270-00450.
